--- title: "How is it cut out and put together?" --- Every part flattened from the model's own tables and nested on one sheet, then written out at 1:1. The outlines are generated here rather than drawn, so the template cannot drift from the aircraft the rest of the chapter analyses. ::: {.callout-tip} ## Specified **Sheet: A3, 27 g** · from the original brief · it sets both the mass and the space available, so it decides the nesting. **Output: a scale layout plus a true 1:1 PDF** · asked of the user, 2026-08-30 · the PDF is the usable artefact; the figure is what makes the entry readable. ::: ::: {.callout-note} ## Assumed The two fuselage laminations are spliced at different stations so the butt joints are bridged by continuous material in the other layer. The original plan interlocks a single pair of pieces with zigzag teeth instead; staggering is simpler to cut and stronger in a laminate. Cut lines are the finished outline — no allowance is added for the knife. ::: ::: {#5dc0a778 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} MM, A3 = 1e3, (420.0, 297.0) # mm, the specified sheet, landscape SPLIT_A, SPLIT_B = 0.2665, 0.1800 # m, staggered splice stations parts = { "wing": sym_surface(wing_eta, wing_c, b_w / 2), "stabilizer": sym_surface(stab_eta, stab_c, b_h / 2), "fin": fin_outline(), "fuselage A, nose": fuselage_outline(0, SPLIT_A), "fuselage A, tail": fuselage_outline(SPLIT_A, l_fus), "fuselage B, nose": fuselage_outline(0, SPLIT_B), "fuselage B, tail": fuselage_outline(SPLIT_B, l_fus), } # nest() raises if anything falls off the sheet or two parts overlap, so a bad # template stops the render rather than reaching the printer. placed = nest(parts, { "wing": (10, 8), "fin": (320, 8), "stabilizer": (10, 113), "fuselage B, tail": (160, 113), "fuselage A, nose": (10, 184), "fuselage B, nose": (10, 228), "fuselage A, tail": (200, 228), }, A3) foam = S_w + S_h + S_v + 2 * S_fus PDF = "chapters/02-mceagle-300/mceagle-300-cutting-plan-a3.pdf" ``` ::: **Answer.** All seven pieces fit one A3 sheet, using 46% of its area and 12\.52 g of its 27\.0 g — so one sheet builds the glider with more than half left over. The fuselage is the constraint. At 437\.6 mm it overhangs A3's 420 mm edge by 17\.6 mm, so it cannot be cut in one piece — which is precisely why the original plan splits its fuselage and interlocks the halves. The same constraint reappears at this scale. Here it is cut as two laminations spliced 87 mm apart, so each butt joint is backed by unbroken foam in the other layer. [**Download the 1:1 cutting plan (A3 PDF)**](mceagle-300-cutting-plan-a3.pdf) — print at 100%, not "fit to page", and check the printed wing measures 300 mm tip to tip before cutting anything. ::: {#cell-fig-cutting .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} def draw(ax): for n, p in placed.items(): ax.fill(p[:, 0], p[:, 1], facecolor="none", edgecolor="k", lw=0.6) ax.set_xlim(0, A3[0]); ax.set_ylim(0, A3[1]) ax.set_aspect("equal"); ax.axis("off") # The 1:1 artefact: an A3 page with one drawing unit to the millimetre. pdf = plt.figure(figsize=(A3[0] / 25.4, A3[1] / 25.4)) draw(pdf.add_axes([0, 0, 1, 1])) pdf.savefig(PDF); plt.close(pdf) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5.7)) draw(ax) ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle((0, 0), *A3, fill=False, ec="0.6", lw=1)) for n, p in placed.items(): ax.text(p[:, 0].mean(), p[:, 1].mean(), n, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=6.5, color="0.45") plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![The seven parts nested on one A3 sheet. Drawn from the model's own chord tables and depth profile, and written out at 1:1 as the linked PDF.](2026-08-30-01-how-is-it-cut-out-and-put-together_files/figure-html/fig-cutting-output-1.png){#fig-cutting width=1175 height=840} ::: ::: ::: {#tbl-build .cell tbl-cap='Where each part goes, measured from the nose along the fuselage\'s straight top edge.' execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd x_np = neutral_point() m_b = ballast_for(x_np - 0.10 * c_w, 0.0) mp = mass_properties(m_ballast=m_b, x_ballast=0.0) pd.DataFrame({ "step": ["laminate the fuselage", "wing leading edge", "wing dihedral", "stabilizer trailing edge", "stabilizer incidence", "fin trailing edge", "nose ballast", "check: balance point"], "where / how much": [ f"2 layers, splices {abs(SPLIT_A-SPLIT_B)*MM:.0f} mm apart", f"{x_le_w*MM:.1f} mm aft of the nose", f"tips {z_tip*MM:.1f} mm above the centre ({dihedral:.1f}°)", f"{x_te_v*MM:.1f} mm — flush with the tail, underneath", f"{i_h:.0f}° (trailing edge up)", f"{x_te_v*MM:.1f} mm — flush with the tail, on top", f"{m_b*1e3:.2f} g at the nose", f"{mp.x_cg*MM:.1f} mm aft of the nose", ], }).style.hide(axis="index") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
step where / how much
laminate the fuselage 2 layers, splices 87 mm apart
wing leading edge 93.4 mm aft of the nose
wing dihedral tips 34.5 mm above the centre (13.3°)
stabilizer trailing edge 437.6 mm — flush with the tail, underneath
stabilizer incidence -2° (trailing edge up)
fin trailing edge 437.6 mm — flush with the tail, on top
nose ballast 2.98 g at the nose
check: balance point 149.0 mm aft of the nose
``` ::: ::: **Assembly.** Cut all seven pieces, marking the forward direction on each. Laminate the two fuselage layers face to face with the splices offset, and let them dry flat under a weight. Glue the stabilizer under the tail and the fin on top of it, both trailing edges flush with the square end, and set the stabilizer 2° trailing-edge-up relative to the wing — that negative incidence is what lifts the nose out of a stall. Divide the wing along its centreline, sand about 10 mm of each cut edge to a 13\.3° bevel, and glue the halves back together on top of the fuselage with the leading edge 93\.4 mm aft of the nose, propping the tips 34\.5 mm up while it dries. The finished wing spans 292 mm across the tips even though 300 mm of foam went into it — the dihedral takes the difference. Finally add 2\.98 g at the nose and check it balances 149\.0 mm back. Balance is the one thing worth measuring rather than trusting: everything else tolerates a millimetre, and this does not. ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## The method, as called ```python def sym_surface(eta, chord, semi): """ A symmetric flat pattern [mm]: straight leading edge, chord table swept to both tips. Span along x, chord along y -- paper is landscape, so are wings. """ y = np.concatenate([-eta[::-1], eta[1:]]) * semi * 1e3 c = np.concatenate([chord[::-1], chord[1:]]) * 1e3 return np.column_stack([np.concatenate([y, y[::-1]]), np.concatenate([np.zeros_like(y), c[::-1]])]) def fin_outline(): """The fin's flat pattern [mm]: straight trailing edge, swept leading edge.""" z, c = fin_eta * b_v * 1e3, fin_c * 1e3 return np.column_stack([np.concatenate([np.zeros_like(z), -c[::-1]]), np.concatenate([z, z[::-1]])]) def fuselage_outline(x0, x1): """ A slice of the fuselage plate between two stations [mm]. The top edge is straight -- it is what carries the wing -- and the belly hangs below it, so the outline is the depth profile mirrored about y = 0. """ xs = np.linspace(x0, x1, 200) d = np.interp(xs, fus_x, fus_d) return np.column_stack([np.concatenate([xs, xs[::-1]]) * 1e3, np.concatenate([np.zeros_like(xs), -d[::-1]]) * 1e3]) def nest(parts, layout, sheet): """ Place parts at given bottom-left corners and check the packing. Raises rather than returning a flag: a template that overhangs the sheet or overlaps itself is worse than no template, and it should stop the render. """ placed = {n: p - p.min(axis=0) + np.array(layout[n]) for n, p in parts.items()} bb = lambda p: (p[:, 0].min(), p[:, 1].min(), p[:, 0].max(), p[:, 1].max()) for n, p in placed.items(): x0, y0, x1, y1 = bb(p) if x0 < 0 or y0 < 0 or x1 > sheet[0] or y1 > sheet[1]: raise ValueError(f"{n} falls off the {sheet[0]:.0f}x{sheet[1]:.0f} sheet") names = list(placed) for i, a in enumerate(names): for b in names[i + 1:]: ax0, ay0, ax1, ay1 = bb(placed[a]) bx0, by0, bx1, by1 = bb(placed[b]) if ax0 < bx1 and bx0 < ax1 and ay0 < by1 and by0 < ay1: raise ValueError(f"{a} overlaps {b}") return placed ``` :::
